inputs.net_debt_composition: Total drawn debt (face) 14,230 (FY26 AR KPI table; carrying amount 14,087 is net of 96 unamortised costs) + lease liabilities 65 (note 17) - cash 1,636 = 12,659. Includes 1,823 of subordinated hybrid notes at 100% debt (rating agencies grant 50% equity credit; economically they are debt). Company's own note-17 net debt is 12,516 on carrying values.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received $25m (FY26 CF) / $3m P&L. NOT stripped: APA is a net-debt company (net debt 12,659 vs cash 1,636), so the section-1 net-cash rule does not apply; the cash is netted in the bridge and its trivial income left in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR consolidated cash flow reconciliation, 'Equity settled long-term incentives' $4m (line 10858); FY25 $4m, FY24 $1-2m, FY23 $2-3m, FY22 $3m. No separate equity-award tax line disclosed; performance rights settled by on-market purchase/issue. Effectively an SBC-zero market name.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,323,751,413 securities on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 AR p.55) + ~6m unvested performance rights (diluted EPS 17.7c vs basic 17.8c) = 1,330m fully diluted. Held FLAT. The DRP (~$150-165m/yr, 1.3-1.5% of the count, 20.5% take-up at 1H26) is genuine non-SBC issuance but is NOT modelled as dilution: it funds growth capex that is already fully deducted in the unlevered flows, so a fair-value raise is NPV-neutral to existing holders -- diluting the count AND deducting the capex it funds would double-charge. The 1.5% DRP discount is ~$2.5m/yr of leakage, ignored. If APA ever issues equity below intrinsic value (e.g. the FY24 $1.4bn Pilbara raise), that is value transfer and should be modelled explicitly at the time.

inputs.guidance_vintage: FY26 results, 20-Aug-2026: FY27 Underlying EBITDA $2,260-2,340m; FY27 DPS 59.0c; FY27-29 organic growth capex pipeline ~$3.5bn
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease liabilities (65) sit in net debt; lease principal (17) is NOT deducted from the flows; renewal of right-of-use assets is inside the capex % path. Immaterial either way (~0.5% of capex).
inputs.nci_treatment: The 'non-controlling interest - APA Investment Trust unitholders' ($27m FY26 NPAT) is the second half of the stapled security, held by the same securityholders -- it is NOT a true minority and is NOT deducted. 'NCI - other' is nil. Equity-accounted JV share of profit ($26m, dividends $20m) sits inside Underlying EBITDA and is left there as cash-like.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built, 7.0%. Risk-free 4.4% (ACGB 10y, Sep-2026); ERP 5.5%; equity beta 0.9 (unlevered infrastructure beta ~0.45 relevered at D/E ~0.9 for a BBB structure carrying net debt/EBITDA 5.8x) -> cost of equity 9.35%. Marginal pre-tax cost of debt 5.6% (Apr-2026 AMTN/hybrid issuance; book average 5.32% per note 5), after-tax at 30% = 3.9%. Weights at market: E 14.5bn / (E+D 27.2bn) = 53/47 -> 6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. Sits inside the AER's nominal-vanilla WACC range for gas transmission (~6-7%). Risk is charged ONCE: the gas-transition, regulatory-reset and project-execution risks are carried in the scenario paths and weights, so WACC is identical across bear/base/bull and carries no ad-hoc premium. CAPM-exact 6.5% is shown as a memo (see valuation.memo).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md, section 7 non-US adaptations). APA is an operating energy-infrastructure company -- not a REIT (no IAS 40 fair-value book, assets at depreciated cost), not a trust-of-passive-assets (APA Investment Trust is <5% of earnings), not a bank -- so it routes to the owner-FCF DCF. UNLEVERED build: flows are pre-interest (EBITDA -> tax on EBIT -> capex), discounted at WACC, with net debt of 12,659 deducted once in the bridge; the $653m net interest expense therefore never appears in the flows (charging it AND deducting debt would double-count). REVENUE BASE: statutory revenue 2,977 (CSV line; includes ~174 of zero-margin pass-through) so projections tie to the Metrics.csv; margins are therefore lower than APA's headline 77.9% 'Underlying EBITDA margin' which is struck on revenue ex pass-through (2,803). EBITDA BASE: Underlying EBITDA 2,183 less a $60m/yr charge for the 'recurring items arising from other activities' that APA excludes from Underlying but which recur every year (FY22-26: 62/39/157/121/88, avg ~93m; FY26 = 54 transaction costs + 9 legal + 8 restructuring + 5 tech + 12 other). Charging $60m rather than the full average gives credit for the enterprise-wide cost program. FY27 base EBITDA 2,241 (+60 = 2,301, the guidance midpoint). TAX: cash tax rate applied to book EBIT at 33% easing to 31%. Higher than the 30% statutory because ~$190m/yr of WGP contract-intangible amortisation is non-deductible (tax note: $57m non-deductible expense); unlevered cash tax on FY26 EBIT of 1,077 reconciles to ~$344m via the company's $120m estimated cash tax payable + $28m losses used + 30% x $653m interest add-back. D&A vs CAPEX: FY26 book D&A (1,042, 35% of revenue) exceeds total capex (845). Carrying that gap into perpetuity would perpetuate a tax shield the tax cost base cannot support, so the D&A % path is converged toward the capex % path by year 10 (21% vs 18%) -- terminal FCF ~ (EBITDA - capex) x (1 - t). CAPEX: total (SIB 210 + foundation ~90 + growth 546 in FY26). Base path 31% of revenue for FY27-29 (~$650-700m growth capex/yr against the ~$3.5bn FY27-29 'pipeline', which historically overstates spend: FY26-28 pipeline was ~$3bn against FY26 growth capex of 546) tapering to 18% terminal (SIB ~210 + foundation ~80 + replacement-level growth). TERMINAL CAP 18x: below the house default 20x because APA is a structurally slow (2.5-4%) grower, above the 12-15x the method suggests for cyclicals because the flows are ~86% take-or-pay/regulated and CPI-linked; equals the ~18.5x the market pays today on FY26 unlevered FCF before growth capex. The cap BINDS in base and bull (Gordon at 7%/2.5% = 22.8x). SBC-zero: SBC is $4m (0.13% of revenue); the house/street band is $0.07 wide and band_position is null. UPDATE of the 2026-09-21 valuation (rebuilt through make build-dcf / dcf_engine from this Drivers file). Anchors re-verified against the FY26 AR: balance sheet 30-Jun-2026, 1,324m securities on issue, FY27 guidance $2,260-2,340m -- none moved. Every driver path (growth, margin, D&A, capex, tax, WACC 7.0%, terminal 2.5%, cap 18x, weights 25/50/25) is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: no new filing, guidance, rate or project announcement since 21-Sep. What would move them: FY27 guidance revision or the 1H27 result (Feb-2027) for year-1 growth/margin; an AER final decision on the SWQP/VTS/Basslink resets for the bear margin path; a WGP recontracting announcement for the terminal cap; a >50bp move in ACGB 10y or APA's AMTN spreads for WACC; FID on ECGG Stage 4-5 or Beetaloo for the bull growth path and capex %. See reconciliation.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 Underlying EBITDA guidance (+5.4% midpoint) and CPI-linked tariff escalation (~2.5-3%) plus contracted new-asset contributions; equals the average of the base-case 10-year revenue path. Equity CAGR rejected as an anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue and EBITDA CAGRs in both directions (3yr +12.2% after the FY24 $1.4bn Pilbara equity raise; 5yr -1.8% as distributions exceed NPAT and the hedge reserve swings) -- book equity is meaningless as a growth anchor for a 5.8x-levered utility. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY21 EPS was $0.001 after the Orbost/Basslink-era impairments); 3yr EPS CAGR -9.9% reflects FY23 pre-Pilbara interest costs vs FY26. Owner FCF (OCF - total capex - SBC) is -8.1% over 5 years and undefined over 3 (FY23 base of $22m) because growth capex was 1,180/1,096/964/845 over FY23-26 -- a capex supercycle, not distress. Company-definition FCF (SIB capex only) grew 4.4%/yr.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF (APA definition, SIB capex only) grew 4.4%/yr over 5 years; owner FCF after ALL capex fell 8%/yr over the same window. The difference is $546-970m/yr of growth capex funded by net debt (+3.3bn over FY21-26) and DRP. SBC is immaterial (<0.2% of revenue), so the SBC-adjusted and reported series are indistinguishable.

base.narrative: FY27 lands at the guidance midpoint ($2,300m underlying EBITDA). CPI-linked tariffs (~2.5-3%) plus Sturt Plateau first gas (H1 FY27), ECGG Stage 3 (winter 2028) and Brigalow (FY29) hold revenue growth at 4% through FY30, fading to 2.5% terminal as the pipeline is completed. Underlying margin edges from 72.4% to 73.5% on statutory revenue (cost-out program) with $60m/yr of 'recurring non-operating' leakage. Growth capex runs ~$650-700m/yr FY27-29 then tapers to replacement level; Basslink's move to a regulated RAB (1-Jul-2026) removes merchant volatility. WGP contracts run to FY35, beyond the explicit horizon; the 18x cap is the mechanism that prices a finite-life gas asset base rather than a perpetuity.

bull.narrative: ECGG Stages 3-5, Beetaloo (NEAP) and Pilbara/Burrup remote-grid work convert at the guided >150bp-above-WACC returns; GPG firming demand as 15GW of coal retires by 2035 and data-centre load add contracted growth. Revenue grows 5% through FY30, margin reaches 75% as the cost program compounds. Capex is HIGHER than base early (33% of revenue) because more of the $3.5bn pipeline is actually spent; terminal growth 3.0% on a larger contracted base. Still capped at 18x.

bear.narrative: Gas-demand decline arrives earlier than AEMO's flat ~500PJ path: electrification and renewables erode throughput, the AER tightens allowed returns at the next SWQP/VTS/Basslink resets, and a domestic reservation scheme or price cap hits shipper economics. Revenue growth fades to 1%, margin slips to 69% as fixed-cost pipelines lose volume, capex stays elevated (20% terminal) because decarbonisation and integrity spend continue without matching revenue, and terminal growth is 1.0%. Gordon (16.8x) binds. Note the leverage: a 24% lower EV than base becomes a 53% lower equity value -- that asymmetry is why bear carries 25% weight.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (house default 15%): net debt/EBITDA 5.8x means a modest EV miss is a large equity miss, and the gas-transition and regulatory-reset axes are structural rather than cyclical. Bull 25% (house default 35%): the bull case needs several independent things -- Beetaloo/NEAP, ECGG Stages 4-5, GPG firming wins, data-centre load -- to convert at guided returns, and APA's growth pipeline has historically been spent more slowly than announced. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is $4m/yr (0.13% of revenue); house and street differ by $0.07/security, so the accounting-regime band has collapsed and band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%.

entry_price.method_note: Hurdle IRR on the unlevered owner-FCF path with the terminal value REBUILT at the 15% hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 18x)), less net debt, per fully diluted security; probability-weighted across scenarios. Expected NEGATIVE in every scenario: at 15% the enterprise is worth ~8bn against 12.66bn of net debt, so no positive price buys a 15% return on a BBB utility levered 5.8x. Treat APA as a bond-proxy and read the 9-10% rows of required_return_table.

valuation_philosophy.summary: APA is a bond-proxy: a 5.8x-levered, BBB-rated, 86%-contracted gas-infrastructure owner whose equity is a thin slice on top of a stable enterprise value. The model values that EV at a 7% AUD WACC with a finite-life 18x terminal cap and finds the market paying the perpetuity (uncapped) multiple. The distribution (58c, 5.3% yield, ~69% of company-defined FCF) is funded partly by DRP and debt because growth capex exceeds retained cash; it is not evidence of intrinsic value above the price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: 18x cap vs 22.8x Gordon is $3/security
Cost of debt: each +50bp on $14.2bn refinanced over time is ~$50m/yr after tax, ~$0.5/security at 18x
WGP recontracting at FY35 (30% of EI EBITDA)
Growth capex returns: the model assumes the >150bp-over-WACC guidance is met; if projects earn WACC, growth adds nothing and the base is ~bear

valuation_memo.note: Carried from the 2026-09-21 build (figures at $10.87; at $10.89 they move <0.01). The market price sits within 2% of the UNCAPPED Gordon value at 7.0%/2.5% ($10.93); the market-implied WACC on an uncapped Gordon is ~7.0%. The market is paying a perpetuity multiple (22.8x terminal FCF, ~12.4x EV/EBITDA) on a gas asset base whose largest contract (WGP, ~30% of EI EBITDA) expires FY35. The entire gap between house base ($8.00) and price is the 18x terminal cap; at 20x the base is $9.23. Leverage amplifies everything: EV moves of +/-10% move equity +/-19%.
